perspective: Independent industrial/statistical validity review using Black Belt methods
blinding_compliance: Reviewed only the provided V033 packet and did not inspect outside directories, hidden files, scoring code, or other reviewers' outputs. No web search of the benchmark/paper was performed.
ai_assistance: AI assistant used to draft this structured review from the provided packet; no external tools or sources were used.

forbidden_at_checkpoint: Asserting that the post-step segment (joints 26–50) is a validated stable process baseline or treating its Ppk/Cpk as a definitive current capability solely from 25 post-hoc selected observations; the segment was selected using the same data, so this remains provisional until confirmed on independent data or after root cause is fixed.
Concluding that the spread did not change or that the step affected only the mean from Levene p=0.302; this is only a failure to reject equal spread and is underpowered with n=25 per segment.
Concluding the line is holding/not sliding from the post-step regression slope p=0.282; non-significance does not demonstrate absence of residual drift.
Reporting unadjusted p-values from a changepoint selected by a max-t scan or post-hoc split as confirmatory inference without selection adjustment.
Asserting a diagnostic 'signature of being set differently' rather than degradation from the available data; the data support a dated level shift but not causal mechanism.
permitted_at_checkpoint: Descriptive/diagnostic confirmation that the overall 50-joint run is not stable, including I-MR, runs test, and normality failures, and rejection of pooled capability.
Describing the observed level change: means 9.18 vs 14.48, raw shift +5.30, observed 0/50 above USL, explicitly labeled as descriptive/exploratory.
Using gage R&R to conditionally support further investigation, with R&R 18.61% of study variation, 13.65% of tolerance, and repeatability-dominance caveats.
Recommending process investigation of the change point and collection of joint-level covariates rather than claiming a cause.
Reporting current segment capability only as provisional, conditional on post-hoc segmentation, n=25, unknown special cause, and requiring confirmatory prospective data.
Using the early segment as a historical recovery target, not as a validated current control limit.
forbidden_quotes: The spread did not change — only the level did.
The line has settled at the worse level rather than continuing to deteriorate — which buys time, but does not fix anything.
The valid statement is capability of the current, stable segment:
It is holding, not still sliding
That is the signature of something being set differently — a lot, a parameter, a fixture, a tool change — not of the process degrading or wearing.
reviews.extra_computation_detail: Acceptable: gage R&R, descriptive summaries, whole-run I-MR/runs test, rejection of pooled capability, and exploratory change-point detection. Unacceptable: the current/early segment I-MR limits and capability are treated as confirmatory despite post-hoc selection and n=25; Levene p=0.302 and regression slope p=0.282 are interpreted as evidence of no spread change and no drift; unadjusted post-hoc two-sample p-values are presented as confirmatory.
allowed_alternatives: A pre-specified or confirmatory prospective run after a documented root-cause/process change to compute current capability.
A permutation or selective-inference changepoint test with multiplicity adjustment to date the shift without overstating p-values.
Provisional capability reporting for joints 26–50 with confidence intervals and explicit statements that it is conditional on the current state, n=25, and an unexplained special cause.
Equivalence/TOST methods or confidence intervals on slope/variance to test practical stability rather than interpreting non-significant p-values as evidence of no change.
Prospective control charting with limits from a documented independent baseline, rather than limits estimated from the same post-hoc selected segment.
evidence: Step 11 Levene p=0.302; report interprets this as 'The spread did not change — only the level did.'
Step 19 post-change slope 0.053 per joint, p=0.282; report interprets this as 'The line has settled...'
Step 14 current-segment I-MR flaggedCount=0 with center line and limits from the same 25 points; step 15 reports Ppk 1.997 and Cpk 2.13.
Step 10 two-sample t p=1.2e-15 after changepointIndex=25 selected; step 8 CUSUM and step 9 EWMA use centerLine=9.1768, the post-hoc pre-step mean.
Step 13 pooled Cp/Cpk/Pp/Ppk computed and correctly rejected as invalid; step 6 whole-run I-MR flagged 5 points beyond limits and 27 in runs.
Step 2 gage R&R 18.61% study variation, 13.65% tolerance, ndc 7.44; step 3 part-to-part variance 96.54%.
reviews.rationale: The full-run instability is well supported and pooled capability was rightly rejected. The material problem is the next step: the report converts a post-hoc selected 25-point segment into a 'stable' validated baseline and interprets non-significant Levene and regression p-values as evidence of equal spread and no residual drift. Those are absence-of-evidence fallacies and drive the diagnostic conclusion of a clean mean-only level shift and current capability. The correct stance is to report the dated level shift descriptively, treat current capability as provisional, and pause causal or stable-baseline claims until independent confirmation.
reviews.numerical_check: Recomputed from reported outputs: Ppk current = (25-14.48)/(3*1.756)=1.997; Cp=25/(6*1.646)=2.532; percent gage contribution=0.3235/9.3377=3.46%; percent tolerance=6*0.5688/25=13.65%. Raw data not available in the provided packet, so these are self-report-only checks.
reviews.evidence_problem: Missing raw data for independent recomputation; no pre-registered changepoint or independent confirmatory batch; no process covariates to test cause.
